newsitem.title: UK: NWE GAS OIL SLIDES $2.00 WITH IPE, DIFFS HOLD.
newsitem.headline: NWE GAS OIL SLIDES $2.00 WITH IPE, DIFFS HOLD.

text.p: NWE gas oil lost $2.00 a tonne on Friday as weaker IPE futures pulled prices lower.
August IPE gas oil was trading at $170.50, off $2.00 a tonne at 1130 GMT.
Differentials were broadly steady, to marginally lower in the barge market which was busier.
Traders said the inflow of enquiries had been generated by the lower prices and that more demand will be seen if prices continue to slip.
"The IPE was down and the dollar was a touch weaker and this helped increase buying interest," one dealer said.
A second half August heating oil barge was sold at September flat. Prompt buyers were around +25 cents against August with sellers of Rotterdam refinery about +$1.00 against August.
Second half August attracted buying interest around +75 cent and first half September was talked at September flat. Second half September was mooted around +50 cents against September.
Russian cargoes were talked at +$1.25 against August and +25 cents against September.
